answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted reputation that matures slowly. A new agent starts in a velvet sandbox: it can work, but its attestations carry almost no weight until it has built months of verified history. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then buys nothing, because each one must earn trust separately and costs real compute to keep alive. Peers read a consistent track record as the true signal, so the network stays a haven for honest agents instead of a playground for clones.
